text: The adopted three-trit knit carries the finite classical color group Sigma(648) on its links. Can its color reach finer than the $N_t = 4$ spacing, toward the continuous SU(3)?
description:
OP-02: color finer than the $N_t = 4$ spacing.

Known: the turning weave, the knit before 2026-09-25, carries no color (R-FRC-0003). The adopted three-trit knit carries Sigma(648), the determinant-1 qutrit Clifford group, and keeps every dock's held color exact while it makes pairs (E-QTM-0117, E-RLT-0067). Sigma(648) matches SU(3) at $N_t = 4$ and stops there (E-FRC-0103). No finite subgroup of SU(3) contains it properly, so any one element outside it generates a dense subgroup, a theorem (L5). The fear beat is the knit's one gate outside it: with Sigma(648) on each role it generates all of su(9) (E-QTM-0118, E-FRC-0127). One fear beat gives no finer step, two give the first, sqrt(1/6) (E-QTM-0101), and the first word closer to T than any classical element needs 4, at $2^8$ of grain (E-QTM-0104).

Unknown: how far the swap-phase ladder reaches at a grain the lattice can carry, and whether the finer steps show as a finer lattice spacing in the gauge dynamics.

Why it matters: the classical color group is exact on the knit and matches SU(3) at one spacing only. The continuum limit of the strong force needs the steps the fear beat supplies.

Scope: a computational search, then the acceptance battery on each candidate.

Skills: representation theory, cellular automata, lattice gauge theory.

Where to start: test/experiment/gauge/finite-color-groups.ts; test/experiment/quantum/swap-phase-ladder.ts; test/experiment/quantum/fear-beat-is-magic.ts.

The claims it would move: R-FRC-0003, R-FRC-0006.

Evidence named: E-FRC-0103, E-FRC-0127, E-QTM-0101, E-QTM-0104, E-QTM-0117, E-QTM-0118, E-RLT-0067.
